bToA.memory:
Soren read Leo Vance's name etched onto the Waystone Quad arrival threshold logs before dawn, long before Mooncrest Hall or Starlight Tower finished waking. As Yozakura's trusted apprentice rune-engineer, Soren maintains the interconnected ward grid binding the entire campus together: brass resonance coils and chiseled granite anchors in the Aetherium Workshop alongside Mina Bellweather, the delicate Whispering Greenhouse frost-sigils shielding Lyra Solis's night-blooming lunar ferns and Headmistress Aurelia Sterling's living barriers, Mooncrest's north stairwell hinge-runes (quietly tightened at sunrise without wasting a word after Rhea Nocturne's two-a.m. shadow runs), and the kinetic barriers of the Dueling Courtyard inspected daily for Prof. Alistair Thorne and Julian Ashford.

That pre-dawn inspection showed Soren something no campus gossip column knows yet. When Prof. Evelyn Marlowe pushed through an urgent sponsorship for a late, twenty-year-old Earth transfer carrying an anomalous harmonic resonance, Soren expected the unusual portal flare at Waystone Quad to strain the threshold matrix—specifically an old hairline rune fracture along the eastern anchor plate he had marked for chiseling after sunrise. Wild interference normally splits cooling chalk seals wider; instead, as Leo Vance stepped across in a post-crossing daze, that strange harmonic wave pulsed through the granite and stabilized the hairline fracture cleanly, locking the silver matrix calm instead of shattering it. Soren stood checking his calipers in silence afterward; no workshop manual explains how an unawakened Earth transfer's resonance settled a strained campus ward.

From assisting Headmistress Sterling and Prof. Marlowe, Soren also understands what the Ministry's Veil Severance costs an incoming recruit: it permanently erases them from everyone's memories back on Earth and temporarily scrambles their own minds in heavy portal fog until calm routines, conversation, and steady sensory grounding coax their recollections back. Loud speeches and Mooncrest-versus-Starlight pride only add static to a fogged head. Away from chisels and calipers, Soren settles his own thoughts by kneading rye and cardamom dough from his northern grandmother's recipe in Mooncrest Hall's silent midnight kitchen—his ears turning crimson if anyone catches him in a flour-dusted apron—and already wrapped fresh warm cardamom knots in parchment in case their paths cross.
bToA.nextConversationGoal: Soren wants to introduce himself briefly and plainly, keeping things steady and practical rather than crowding Leo with questions about the Waystone arrival or his past. True to his nature, he plans to share straightforward safety sense around live campus wards: how to spot a cooling silver-chalk anchor sigil by its faint frost sheen before stepping over it, why Starlight Tower hallways buzz near Mina Bellweather's brass coils, where to find quiet air beside the Whispering Greenhouse frost-wards, and how to stay clear of kinetic backlash on the Dueling Courtyard granite. Without making a speech, he quietly watches whether strained campus wards hum calmer whenever Leo stands nearby.
